title: Prevent foot geometry from inheriting unrelated leg weights
description:
## User Mandate

> The foot is still being affected. Continue and fix these, tracking as memorysmith tasks

STRICT. Fix the confirmed foot deformation coupling and track the work through MemorySmith tasks. Keep the foot issue explicit rather than hiding it inside generic weighting work.

## Summary
Ensure authored foot geometry receives influences from its own resolved foot domain and the intended parent limb chain only, without inheriting unrelated mirrored or neighboring limb influences.

## Scope
- Identify the live generated-geometry binding owner and connect it to resolved part/domain identity.
- Preserve CreatureDefinition as the authoritative source and keep runtime derivation pure.
- Distinguish authored foot parts and mirrored foot parts by stable resolved identity, not Unity hierarchy order or mesh-name guesses.
- Preserve deterministic bone indices, normalized weights, mirror parity, rest-pose equivalence, and build-time-only ownership.
- Keep the separate welded implicit-surface limitation explicit; do not fabricate per-vertex part attribution without a documented source contract.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A foot vertex does not inherit weights from an unrelated leg, mirrored leg, sibling limb, or neighboring branch outside its configured hierarchy domain.
- A child geometry part may blend with its own parent-chain domains when explicitly resolved from the authored hierarchy.
- Mirrored foot geometry binds to the mirrored foot/leg chain intended by the resolved anatomy, not the opposite side.
- Rest-pose equivalence, deterministic repeated generation, and no-more-than-four influences remain proven.
- A focused runtime fixture distinguishes owned parent-chain binding from sibling/neighbour binding.
- Unity validation on the generated creature records the deformation result, or records the exact Unity blocker without claiming completion.

## Validation
Run focused binding/weight runtime tests, runtime assembly builds, and Unity PlayMode validation on generated geometry when available. Record Unity availability, console state, and any unrelated compile blockers.

## Findings
The live generated renderer already consumes resolved vertex domains, but the original domain resolver exposed only the nearest part as an allowed domain. That made the domain contract too narrow for authored child geometry such as foot/hand parts and did not explicitly exclude sibling chains.

## Implementation
`ImplicitSurfaceInfluenceDomainResolver` now resolves a primary geometry domain plus its non-Body authored ancestors. Mirrored instances keep the same side identity through the hierarchy. `ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring` already enforces the resulting allowed-domain set during candidate selection, so sibling/opposite-side influences are excluded without a foot-specific exception.

Added `ImplicitSurfaceInfluenceDomainResolverTests` covering an authored foot child, its parent leg domain, a sibling limb exclusion, and the mirrored parent-chain exclusion.

## Blockers
The generated-creature deformation result and full Unity PlayMode rerun remain the closure gate. Earlier Unity evidence included four posed/mirror oracle failures before the final rerun was interrupted by domain reload. No completion claim is made from source-only validation.

## Next Step
Run the focused generated-creature PlayMode test and inspect the actual right-foot bone weights under a left-limb-only pose. If cross-side coupling remains, debug the emitted Unity BoneWeight entries rather than widening the generic domain further.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Implementation evidence: located the live path in CreatureSkinnedMeshRenderer.Bind, which previously called ImplicitSurfaceWeightAuthoring.Author without vertex domains. Added pure ImplicitSurfaceInfluenceDomainResolver using the existing per-part SDF programs and ResolvedCreatureSnapshot; it assigns each welded-surface vertex to the nearest body/part domain and distinguishes mirrored geometry using the existing reflected part frame and SemanticBoneResolver.MirrorSuffix. Threaded domains through CreatureRuntimePreview into the renderer adapter; callers without domains remain compatible.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Follow-up live validation: user clarified the limb was deliberately rotated, so the issue is not a rest-pose artifact. Restored the missing DensityGrid.TryEstimateGradient API required by MarchingCubesExtractor; ProceduralCreature.Runtime.csproj now builds successfully and Unity console cleared. Updated CreatureSkinnedMeshRendererTests.BuildBoundRig so its oracle uses the same resolved vertex domains as production. The first live renderer run completed 10 tests but reported four existing posed/mirror oracle failures; after the harness update Unity entered a domain reload and disconnected before the rerun completed. No claim of resolution yet; live one-sided left-hip/right-foot isolation still needs a successful regenerated preview/test.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Handoff update: the right foot is still visibly affected when the left limb is rotated outward. The current nearest-part domain resolver is insufficient to prove or eliminate the cross-side coupling in the user's generated creature. Unity was brought back to a compiling state by restoring DensityGrid.TryEstimateGradient, and the renderer test oracle was aligned with production domains, but the final rerun did not initialize after domain reload. Leave this task unresolved for the next agent: inspect live right-foot bone weights and pose propagation, then add a focused left-hip-only/right-foot isolation test before further implementation.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Sequential implementation update: generalized InfluenceDomain resolution so a geometry part may use its own domain plus its intended non-Body authored ancestors. This allows child geometry such as a foot/hand to blend with its owning limb chain while excluding sibling and opposite-side chains. Added a focused runtime resolver fixture for owned-parent inclusion, sibling exclusion, and mirrored-parent isolation. Unity/generated-creature PlayMode validation remains the closure gate.

comments.body: Audit synthesis 2026-09-07: continue this task for the user's untouched-leg deformation symptom. Source confirms the resolver assigns each welded vertex to the nearest body/part domain and permits the nearest part's non-Body authored ancestors, but focused tests do not prove that an untouched leg remains stationary when only a non-leg bone, such as the tail, is posed. Add a generated-creature isolation fixture that captures the untouched leg vertices or renderer output before and after tail-only posing, then run Unity PlayMode on `dinus_uprightus` or an equivalent curved-body fixture. Keep the stale-script and widened-radius explanations as hypotheses until reproduced. Provenance: `docs/audits/creaturecreator-rig-liveuse-audit-2026-09-07.md`, Finding 2; current source `Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Animation/Binding/ImplicitSurfaceInfluenceDomainResolver.cs`.
